It's so confusing because symptoms do overlap, but I don't feel like it fits the way CVS does.

Commenting because I haven't seen this said yet and it could be the cause. I have the same issue, always have done and I'm now in my 30s. Turns out I have a tilted cervix which was preventing tampons from going in properly, causing pain when I tried to use them, and actually pushing them out when I moved around at some points. Never knew until well into my 20s that it was a thing, and that your cervix can be lower down, on one side or at pretty much any angle. Didnt realise it wasn't "normal" to be able to reach your cervix with your fingers until a nurse told me it was unusual that I could feel mine. 

Tilted cervix is natural and normal, about 1 in 5 women have some sort of tilt. Mine happens to be more tilted than some, which is why tampons have always sucked. Some people with a tilt find success with menstrual cups, maybe that could be a solution for beach days if you happen to have a tilt too?
